_comment: SHIPPED WITH THE PLUGIN. The input contract the three commands validate
against, at the door, before anything is spawned.
It is a copy, and the copy is asserted rather than trusted: spec 028 NFR-4
and the RE_* assignments in action/lib.sh identical rule for rule and in both
directions. A regex that moves in any one of the three and not the others
It ships because the published tree carries no specs/ directory, so an
installed plugin cannot read the spec fixture. Collapsing the copies into one
shared module is the spec after 028 (its decision 1).
The runner has had the same contract at its own door since spec 026. This one
runs FIRST: the runner refuses after a process has already started, and the

models.message: models: expected a comma-separated list of model ids (letters, digits, . _ -)

max_usd.message: max-usd: expected a positive decimal number such as 20 or 3.53

max_usd_zero.message: max-usd: must be greater than zero

max_calls.message: max-calls: expected a positive integer with no leading zero

_note: THE PLUGIN'S OWN, and the one rule in this file that action/lib.sh does
not carry — so it declares no bash_name, and spec 028 NFR-4 holds it
between this file and the spec fixture rather than against the Action.
Why the door is stricter here than the Action is. The Action validates a
value it is about to hand to a shell script. This door hands it to an
argv array with shell:false, so the characters below cannot execute
anything through it. They are refused because AC-4 says a person running
on the trusted lane, in their own checkout, should be TOLD about a path
that looks like a command substitution rather than have it quietly work.
Before spec 028 v1.3 only the control-character rule applied here, and
five of AC-4's six payload classes were refused by the existence check
instead — a refusal for a reason that has nothing to do with the
skill_dir_shell_metachar.message: skill-dir: contains a shell metacharacter (a quote, a semicolon, a backtick, or a $( command substitution)
